item.research_question: What are the hot deformation behaviors, dynamic recrystallization mechanisms, and grain refinement capabilities of the Co35Cr25Ni15Mn15Fe10 TRIP-HEA under varying temperatures and strain rates?
item.processing_route: Hot compression of cylindrical samples (12 mm height × 8 mm diameter) to a true strain of 1.0 (63% reduction) at temperatures of 1123, 1173, 1223, and 1273 K with strain rates of 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001 s−1; samples were heated to 1473 K, held for 300 s, cooled to compression temperature, held for 10 s, compressed, and water quenched.
item.test_conditions: Compression temperatures: 1123–1273 K; Strain rates: 0.1–0.001 s−1; True strain: 1.0; Zener–Hollomon parameter (Z) varied by temperature and strain rate.
key_findings: The apparent activation energy for hot deformation was measured to be 385.7 kJ/mol.
The peak flow stress increased with an increase in strain rate and/or a decrease in temperature.
The volume fraction of dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grains ranged from 4.8% (at 1123 K, 0.1 s−1) to 82% (at 1273 K, 0.001 s−1).
The average diameter of DRXed grains ranged from 5 to 20 μm across all investigated conditions.

Discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (dDRX) was predominant at small Zener–Hollomon parameters (high temperature, low strain rate), while continuous dynamic recrystallization (cDRX) prevailed at large Z values.
A necklacelike structure composed of fine equiaxed grains and coarse elongated grains formed at medium Z values.
The constitutive equation showed a linear correlation between ln(sinh(ασ)) and lnZ with a fitting coefficient of 0.994.
Homogeneous grain structures with a size of approximately 19 μm were achieved at 1273 K and 0.001 s−1.
item.mechanism: The flow softening is driven by dynamic recrystallization (both dDRX and cDRX) which consumes stored dislocation energy. dDRX nucleates at grain boundaries via bulging, favored by high temperature and low strain rates due to high grain boundary mobility. cDRX occurs via subgrain formation and rotation, favored by high strain rates and low temperatures where dislocation recovery is impeded. The high activation energy (385.7 kJ/mol) indicates sluggish diffusion, which hinders dynamic recovery and grain growth, leading to higher peak stresses and finer grain sizes compared to conventional alloys.
item.limitations: The study notes that grain growth often occurs at elevated temperatures to minimize grain boundary energy, which can counteract refinement efforts at very high temperatures and low strain rates.
item.future_work: The study provides guidelines for optimizing grain morphology and mechanical properties of the TRIP-HEA through thermomechanical processing such as hot-compression, hot-rolling, and hot-extrusion.
quotes: The apparent activation energy was estimated to be ~385.7 kJ/mol.
The discontinuous dynamic recrystallization played an important role in the grain refinement, particularly at a relatively higher temperature and a lower strain rate.

The cDRX preferentially occurred at a large Zener–Hollomon parameter (low temperature and high strain rate), whereas the dDRX became predominant at a small Zener–Hollomon parameter (high temperature and low strain rate).
